To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the empirical risk function for learning one-hidden layer neural networks with sigmoid activation using cross entropy is strongly convex and smooth in a neighborhood of the ground-truth, (ii) the tensor method can initialize gradient descent to a neighborhood of the true parameter, and (iii) the empirical risk minimizer is close to the ground-truth with high probability, as soon as sample complexity is sufficiently high

(i) under the Gaussian input assumption, the empirical risk minimizer using cross entropy is strongly convex and smooth uniformly over a neighborhood of the ground-truth, as long as the sample size is sufficiently large; (ii) gradient descent initialized in this neighborhood converges linearly, and hence the empirical risk minimizers are guaranteed to converge to a critical point close to the ground-truth; and (iii) the sample size and computational complexity of our algorithm are optimal with respect to the input dimension

the empirical risk function with cross entropy is globally strongly convex and globally Lipschitz smooth, and gradient descent converges globally with linear convergence rate to a global minimizer of the empirical risk function.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish a strong convexity and a smoothness property for the empirical risk function with respect to the weights of the neural network, under Gaussian input.

the empirical risk minimizer of the cross entropy with gradient descent recovers the ground truth with high probability under Gaussian input, and the sample and computational complexity scales linearly with the network input dimension, and is near-optimal.

we establish the global convergence guarantee for the cross entropy loss function using gradient descent for one-hidden-layer neural network recovery, with a sample and computational complexity that is nearly optimal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cross entropy, a popular loss function for training neural networks, can be used for provably recovering the ground truth, and gradient descent is guaranteed to converge to the global optimum.

the cross entropy can serve as a surrogate of the maximum a posteriori probability (MAP) for learning the weights of one-hidden-layer neural network, and gradient descent can recover the ground truth with high probability.

cross entropy, which is the de facto training objective for neural networks in practice, can be used to recover one-hidden-layer neural network weights with provable guarantees, without requiring the training data to be i.i.d. or the network architecture to be sufficiently deep.
